citation.title: Overview of the KSTAR experiments toward fusion reactor
citation.authors: Won-Ha Ko, S.W. Yoon, W.C. Kim, J.G. Kwak, et al. and KSTAR Team

topic: Programmatic overview of recent KSTAR scenarios, RMP ELM control, MHD control, turbulence, divertor and virtual KSTAR work.
own_question: Summarizes recent KSTAR progress toward steady-state, high-beta, long-pulse operation and outlines near-term upgrades.
actual_method_and_evidence: Review of cited experiments and simulations. Examples include a high-li βN≈3 discharge lasting 12 s, a 45 s RMP ELM-control period, ML L-H classification for RMP triggering, ECE/BES-type pedestal fluctuation analyses, and a digital-twin monitoring system. The extracted text does not describe CES nowcasting, CES report latency, or BES/ECEI-to-Ti estimation. Figures were not visually checked.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR has used a real-time ML classifier based on emission and density signals within its plasma control system to trigger RMP after the L-H transition.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a plasma-state classifier, not temperature estimation. The reported 800 µs inference time and 95% validation accuracy are the source's own results and should not be transferred to our study.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR research programs emphasize long-pulse pedestal control, including RMP ELM suppression, where pedestal ion profiles respond to the applied RMPs.
claim_checks.qualification: This is broad context only. The ion-pedestal observations are summarized from other cited work and do not specify the CES species or timing.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not reported for CES. The paper gives no CES arrival time and no impurity-versus-main-ion detail.
forbidden_inferences: CES reports are delayed by a specific amount.
The ML classifier's performance applies to our estimators.
The 2022 campaign data split matches ours.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most an optional citation for general KSTAR long-pulse and real-time PCS motivation. It contains no evidence on our CES nowcasting question, so other, more specific sources are preferable.
